thread:
sara-k: FYI we see a small but consistent NDCG@10 drop (~1.5%) after bringing up the PTQ reranker on canary. It mainly affects short queries (<10 tokens). Running numbers now but wanted to surface for quick triage.
omar: thanks. Is this vs fp16 baseline or the old int8? which holdout?
sara-k: vs fp16 baseline on holdout_A (prod-like). MRR seems flat, ndcg dips. Short queries seem to be majority of the delta. link to summary: https://internal.gists/repro-ptq-smoke (private)
devin-m: do you have an example query+candidate that fails? that often helps rule out tokenization noise
sara-k: paste below (sanitized):

query: "best way to export csv from pandas?"
candidate 1 (gold): "Use df.to_csv('file.csv', index=False) — includes header by default."
candidate 2: "You can use numpy.savetxt if pure arrays."

Both look fine manually but reranker score ordering flips on ptq build.

li-w: quick thought: any chance we're feeding different serializer (html tags/whitespace) into the PTQ path? I remember a parity bug where the preproc used `.strip()` in one pipeline.
omar: good call. Also check tokenizer version and special token handling. PTQ binary might be using a compiled tokenizer with slightly different normalization.
devin-m: can we dump raw token ids for both runs for the failing sample? e.g.

```bash
# quick local diff
python tools/dump_tokens.py --text "best way to export csv from pandas?" --model rerank-v2-fp16 > fp16.tokens
python tools/dump_tokens.py --text "best way to export csv from pandas?" --model rerank-v2-ptq > ptq.tokens
diff fp16.tokens ptq.tokens
```

li-w: also check whether KV cache packing (kvpack) ordering changed — short queries sometimes hit different batching code paths.
sara-k: I ran the token dump for 3 samples. Token ids are identical. So not tokenizer normalization. KV pack suspicion remains.
omar: another angle: quantization scheme. Are we doing per-channel (perout) vs per-tensor? per-channel usually preserves head deltas better.
devin-m: current PTQ artifact was built with per-tensor symmetric 8-bit (fastest). We have a per-channel variant on the build server but we didn't canary it. Could be worth a quick run.
triage-bot: Created issue INF-3421: "ptq-rerank-ndcg-dip-short-queries" and assigned to sara-k, devin-m.
sara-k: proposed small experiment plan:
1) Run the per-channel PTQ binary on holdout_A for short queries subset (<=10 tokens) and compute ndcg@1, ndcg@5, ndcg@10 and MRR.
2) Run the current per-tensor PTQ but with KV pack disabled (force sequential) to see if ordering/packing affects scores.
3) Run a serializer parity test: re-evaluate holdout_A where we canonicalize whitespace/html before sending to both fp16 and ptq pipelines.
Can we split these across people?
omar: I can take 1) — will spin a job on canary GPUs and drop results here.
devin-m: I'll do 2) and try to reproduce locally with `--kvpack=false`. If I can repro locally we can iterate faster.
li-w: I'll help with 3) and prepare a small transform script to canonicalize markup (strip tags, collapse whitespace, normalize quotes). We'll add it as a toggle to eval harness.
sara-k: thanks. timeline: if we can get initial numbers in 24h that'd be great. For tracking add logs to INF-3421 and drop the key diff tables there.
omar: noted. starting job now.
devin-m: local quick check shows ordering flip when kvpack=true; when disabled the scores match fp16 on samples I tried. digging into batch ordering code.
li-w: serializer script ready: `tools/canonicalize_text.py` — I'll run a parity sweep tomorrow morning across holdout_B (clean html) and holdout_A.
sara-k: great. if kvpack is the culprit we should consider a hotfix: keep kvpack but add deterministic slot ordering for short queries or fall back to non-packed path under threshold.
omar: agree. initial job ETA ~3h.
devin-m: will try patch to kvpack ordering invariants; if tests pass I'll open PR and link to INF-3421.
sara-k: perfect. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
triage-bot: INF-3421 updated: "kvpack ordering suspected; per-channel ptq test queued"
